newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares rocked by EMU, U.S. worries.
newsitem.headline: German shares rocked by EMU, U.S. worries.

text.p: Worries about a possible delay for the start of Europe's monetary union and the fate of U.S. interest rates pushed German shares down to a two-week low in a choppy session on Tuesday.
The DAX lost 59.80 points, or 1.8 percent, to end bourse trade at 3,291.19 points, dropping below the psychologically crucial 3,300-point level for the first time since early March.
And despite a brief recovery in the early post-bourse session, the IBIS DAX index of elctronic trade ended the day down 1.42 percent at 3,289.59 points, dragged lower as U.S. shares opened weakly.
Added to EMU and U.S. worries came pressure associated with the expiry later this week of options on the DAX.
"It's been everything together today," said one Frankfurt dealer. "The options expiry seems to be playing havoc with pricing and we need some convincing reassurance from the U.S."

Volumes were relatively moderate with market attention fixed on steelmaker Thyssen, whose shares were suspended from official trade ahead of an announcement which finally came in the afternoon from engineering firm Krupp that it was offering 435 marks for Thyssen shares.

The news raised a storm on the German market, where hostile takeovers are rare, and sent Thyssen shares soaring to an all-time high of 410 marks in unofficial trading. The shares had closed late trade on Monday at 344.50 marks.
"That was a solid price," said one trader of the offer, which slightly exceeded forecasts. Thyssen shares are expected to soar once they resume trade.

Rival engineering firm Preussag also got a boost from the takeover talk as dealers speculated that a merger would cut capacity in the sector. Preussag rose 7.70 marks to 437.70 marks in bourse and ended the day at 441.80 marks.

The chemical sector was weak after Bayer said it would struggle to surpass 1996 profits this year. BASF also ended lower, despite getting a brief boost from 1996 sales and earnings data that were slightly ahead of forecast.
Nonetheless, dealers noted that Germany's big three chemical companies -- which also include Hoechst -- were coming increasingly close on price.
Where previously Hoechst led Bayer, with BASF trailing a very poor third, Bayer ended bourse trade at 68.70 marks on Tuesday, Hoechst was at 67.05 marks and BASF was at 61.51 marks.
